proofs.proof_tex:
For a fixed prefix of length \(\ell\), define its used label dictionary by
\[
 D_\ell=\bigcup_{h=1}^{\ell}S_{\pi(h)}(r_{\pi(h)}),
 \qquad
 A_\ell=D_\ell\cap B_\ell,
 \qquad
 b_\ell=|D_\ell\setminus B_\ell|.
\]
These are exactly the quantities named in \(\text{def:ordered-state}\). We first prove that its transition is exact. If \(\lambda\in D_\ell\setminus B_\ell\), then \(\lambda\) occurs in a processed component. Were it also to occur in an unprocessed component, it would belong to
\[
 \left(\bigcup_{h\leq\ell}U_{\pi(h)}\right)
 \cap
 \left(\bigcup_{h>\ell}U_{\pi(h)}\right)=B_\ell,
\]
which is a contradiction. Thus every label in \(D_\ell\setminus B_\ell\) is absent from every unprocessed component.

Choose a root \(r\in V(T_{\pi(\ell+1)})\), put
\[
 R=S_{\pi(\ell+1)}(r),
 \qquad
 W=A_\ell\cup R,
\]
and let \(D_{\ell+1}=D_\ell\cup R\). The preceding absence property makes the following union disjoint:
\[
 D_{\ell+1}=(D_\ell\setminus B_\ell)\,\dot\cup\,W.
\]
Every label in the first term is absent from all components after \(\ell\), hence also from \(B_{\ell+1}\). Consequently
\[
 D_{\ell+1}\cap B_{\ell+1}=W\cap B_{\ell+1}=A_{\ell+1}
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |D_{\ell+1}\setminus B_{\ell+1}|
 &=|D_\ell\setminus B_\ell|+|W\setminus B_{\ell+1}|\\
 &=b_\ell+|W\setminus B_{\ell+1}|=b_{\ell+1}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves the transition formula in \(\text{def:ordered-state}\) for every prefix.

The same decomposition proves right congruence. Consider two prefixes represented by the same \((A_\ell,b_\ell)\). Their completed labels can differ numerically, but none of those labels occurs in any suffix. For any fixed suffix-root sequence, all labels shared between the prefix and suffix therefore lie in the common set \(A_\ell\), while the two sets of completed labels contribute the same cardinality \(b_\ell\). Applying the displayed transition inductively shows that the two prefixes produce the same state at every later cut and the same final union cardinality. Hence merging equal states loses neither feasibility nor multiplicity information.

At cut zero, \(D_0=B_0=\varnothing\), so the only state is \((\varnothing,0)\). At every cut retain a state only if
\[
 |D_\ell|=|A_\ell|+b_\ell\leq K.
\]
This pruning is sound because extending a prefix can only enlarge its dictionary. Conversely, the transition calculation shows inductively that every prefix whose dictionary has size at most \(K\) reaches its exact retained state. At the final cut, \(B_c=\varnothing\), so \(A_c=\varnothing\) and \(b_c=|D_c|\). Thus the accepting final histories are exactly the tuples \(\rho\) satisfying \(|L(\rho)|\leq K\), namely the elements of \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\). This proves exact feasibility; \(\text{thm:root-union}\) supplies the corresponding causal-orientation interpretation.

For multiplicity, store with each state a count truncated at two and at most two distinct prefix root tuples realizing that count. A root tuple determines one transition history. When histories merge into the same state, right congruence implies that every feasible suffix extends every retained representative of that state. Therefore, if three or more prefixes reach one state, retaining any two distinct representatives preserves the fact that at least two full extensions exist whenever an accepting suffix exists. At the final cut, sum the truncated counts over all accepting states, again truncating at two, and retain two full backpointer chains whenever that sum is two. If the result is zero, the fiber is empty; if it is one, exactly one root tuple is feasible; and if it is two, the two recovered coordinate sequences are distinct feasible root tuples. This proves the claims for \(\textsc{Unique-K-Fiber}\) and \(\textsc{Two-K-Fiber}\), including recovery rather than only decision.

It remains to count retained states. Fix a cut and write \(m=|B_\ell|\). If \(|A_\ell|=i\), retention forces
\[
 0\leq i\leq\min(m,K),
 \qquad
 0\leq b_\ell\leq K-i.
\]
There are \(\binom mi\) possible live sets of size \(i\) and exactly \(K-i+1\) possible completed-label counts. Hence the number of retained states at that cut is at most
\[
 \sum_{i=0}^{\min(m,K)}\binom mi(K-i+1).
\]
Because \(m\leq q_\pi\), embed \(B_\ell\) into a set of size \(q_\pi\). This injects every counted pair \((A_\ell,b_\ell)\) into the pairs counted by
\[
 \mathsf S_{\mathrm{DP}}(q_\pi,K)
 =\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}\binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1),
\]
which proves the sharper state bound.

All root signatures can be precomputed by exact rational arithmetic from \(T\) and \(\Sigma\). From each state there are at most \(|V(T_{\pi(\ell+1)})|\leq p\) transitions. Canonical rational comparisons, indexed finite-set operations, pruning, truncated-count updates, and backpointer updates each require \(\operatorname{poly}(N)\) bit operations. The factors for the \(c\leq p\) cuts and the roots per component are absorbed into \(\operatorname{poly}(N)\). Therefore the total running time is
\[
 \mathsf S_{\mathrm{DP}}(q_\pi,K)\operatorname{poly}(N).
\]
Finally,
\[
 \mathsf S_{\mathrm{DP}}(q_\pi,K)
 \leq (K+1)\sum_{i=0}^{q_\pi}\binom{q_\pi}{i}
 =(K+1)2^{q_\pi},
\]
which recovers the old bound. If \(q_\pi\geq2\), then \(\binom{q_\pi}{i}\leq q_\pi^i\) and hence
\[
 \mathsf S_{\mathrm{DP}}(q_\pi,K)
 \leq (K+1)\sum_{i=0}^{K}q_\pi^i
 \leq (K+1)^2q_\pi^K
 =q_\pi^{O(K)}.
\]
This proves the stated parameterized regime as well as the exact bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \((T,\Sigma,P,K)\in\mathfrak M_{p,K}^{\mathrm{forest}}\) and \(x,y\in V\), the following conclusions hold. If \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)=\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_K(\Sigma;x,y)=\varnothing\). If \(x=y\), every \(\rho\in\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\) satisfies \(\theta_\rho(\Sigma;x,x)=1\). If \(x\) and \(y\) lie in different components of \(T\), every \(\rho\in\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\) satisfies \(\theta_\rho(\Sigma;x,y)=0\). Suppose instead that distinct \(x,y\) lie in component \(T_j\), let \(v\) be the neighbor of \(x\) on the unique \(x\)--\(y\) path, and let \(T_{x;xv}\) denote the vertex set of the component containing \(x\) after deleting the edge \(xv\). Then, for every \(\rho\in\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\),
\[
 \theta_\rho(\Sigma;x,y)=
 \begin{cases}
 \Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx},&r_j\in T_{x;xv},\\
 0,&r_j\notin T_{x;xv}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Moreover \(\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\ne0\), so
\[
 \Theta_K(\Sigma;x,y)\subseteq
 \left\{0,\frac{\Sigma_{yx}}{\Sigma_{xx}}\right\},
\]
with the nonzero value present exactly when a feasible tuple has \(r_j\in T_{x;xv}\), and zero present exactly when a feasible tuple has \(r_j\notin T_{x;xv}\). For a supplied component order, each restricted feasibility condition and a corresponding root-tuple witness are computable in
\[
 \left\{\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}
 \binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\right\}\operatorname{poly}(N)
\]
time; they are also computable in \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\) time when \(d=\max_h|V(T_h)|\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The definition of the effect fiber gives
\[
 \Theta_K(\Sigma;x,y)
 =\{\theta_\rho(\Sigma;x,y):\rho\in\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\}.
\]
Therefore \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)=\varnothing\) immediately implies \(\Theta_K(\Sigma;x,y)=\varnothing\). We now fix \(\rho\in\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\). By \(\text{thm:root-union}\), \(H_\rho\) is the corresponding collider-free forest DAG, and by the definition of \(B_\rho(\Sigma)\), a nonroot vertex \(z\) with its unique parent \(u\) has coefficient
\[
 [B_\rho(\Sigma)]_{zu}
 =\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_P(X_z,X_u)}{\operatorname{Var}_P(X_u)}
 =\frac{\Sigma_{zu}}{\Sigma_{uu}}.
\]
The denominator is strictly positive because \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\).

Since \(H_\rho\) is acyclic, a topological ordering makes \(B_\rho(\Sigma)\) strictly triangular. Hence \(B_\rho(\Sigma)^p=0\) and direct multiplication gives the finite geometric identity
\[
 (I-B_\rho(\Sigma))^{-1}
 =I+B_\rho(\Sigma)+\cdots+B_\rho(\Sigma)^{p-1}.
\]
For \(k\geq1\), the \((y,x)\) entry of \(B_\rho(\Sigma)^k\) is the sum, over directed walks of length \(k\) from \(x\) to \(y\), of the products of their edge coefficients. A directed acyclic graph has no directed walk with a repeated vertex, and the underlying forest has at most one undirected path between two vertices. Thus \(\theta_\rho(\Sigma;x,y)\) is one on the diagonal, is zero when \(x\) and \(y\) are in different components, and for distinct vertices in one component is the product along the unique \(x\)--\(y\) path if that path is directed from \(x\) to \(y\), and zero otherwise. This proves the first three cases, including \(\theta_\rho(\Sigma;x,x)=1\).

Now let distinct \(x,y\) lie in \(T_j\), and write their unique path as
\[
 w_0=x,w_1=v,w_2,\ldots,w_m=y.
\]
The orientation \(H_{j,r_j}\) points away from \(r_j\). After deleting \(xv\), the path from \(r_j\) to \(y\) crosses that edge from \(x\) to \(v\) if and only if \(r_j\in T_{x;xv}\). In that event every edge on the displayed path points from \(w_t\) to \(w_{t+1}\). If \(r_j\notin T_{x;xv}\), its first edge points from \(v\) to \(x\), so the unique path is not directed from \(x\) to \(y\). The path-sum calculation consequently yields
\[
 \theta_\rho(\Sigma;x,y)
 =\begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\prod_{t=0}^{m-1}
 \frac{\Sigma_{w_{t+1}w_t}}{\Sigma_{w_tw_t}},
 &r_j\in T_{x;xv},\\[3mm]
 0,&r_j\notin T_{x;xv}.
 \end{cases}
\]

We derive the asserted simplification of the product from the Gaussian forest law. Faithfulness in \(\text{ass:forest-faithfulness}\) includes the global Markov implication for \(T\). For \(1\leq t<m\), the vertex \(w_t\) separates \(x\) from \(w_{t+1}\) in the forest; hence
\[
 X_x\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{w_{t+1}}\mid X_{w_t}.
\]
For completeness, the scalar Gaussian covariance identity used here follows directly as follows. Put
\[
 R_x=X_x-\frac{\Sigma_{xw_t}}{\Sigma_{w_tw_t}}X_{w_t},
 \qquad
 R_{t+1}=X_{w_{t+1}}
 -\frac{\Sigma_{w_{t+1}w_t}}{\Sigma_{w_tw_t}}X_{w_t}.
\]
The centered vector \((R_x,R_{t+1},X_{w_t})\) is Gaussian, and each residual has zero covariance with \(X_{w_t}\). Its Gaussian density therefore factors between \((R_x,R_{t+1})\) and \(X_{w_t}\). Thus its conditional covariance is the unconditional residual covariance,
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(X_x,X_{w_{t+1}}\mid X_{w_t})
 =\Sigma_{xw_{t+1}}
 -\frac{\Sigma_{xw_t}\Sigma_{w_tw_{t+1}}}{\Sigma_{w_tw_t}}.
\]
Conditional independence makes the left side zero, so
\[
 \Sigma_{xw_{t+1}}
 =\Sigma_{xw_t}
 \frac{\Sigma_{w_tw_{t+1}}}{\Sigma_{w_tw_t}}.
\]
Starting from
\[
 \frac{\Sigma_{xw_1}}{\Sigma_{xx}}
 =\frac{\Sigma_{w_1w_0}}{\Sigma_{w_0w_0}},
\]
and applying the recurrence for \(t=1,\ldots,m-1\) proves by induction that
\[
 \frac{\Sigma_{yx}}{\Sigma_{xx}}
 =\prod_{t=0}^{m-1}
 \frac{\Sigma_{w_{t+1}w_t}}{\Sigma_{w_tw_t}}.
\]
Substitution into the path-product display proves the claimed formula.

The empty set does not separate distinct connected vertices \(x\) and \(y\) in \(T\). Faithfulness therefore implies that \(X_x\) and \(X_y\) are not marginally independent. Their bivariate Gaussian marginal is independent exactly when its off-diagonal covariance is zero, as is seen by factorizing its Gaussian density. Hence \(\Sigma_{yx}\ne0\); positive definiteness also gives \(\Sigma_{xx}>0\). The two displayed candidate effects are consequently distinct. Taking the image over all feasible \(\rho\) now proves both directions of each membership assertion: a tuple on the indicated root side supplies the corresponding value, and the pointwise formula shows that no tuple on the opposite side can supply that value.

It remains to prove the algorithmic assertions. In the ordered dynamic program, when component \(T_j\) is processed, restrict its transition list to roots in \(T_{x;xv}\), or to roots in its complement, respectively. All other transitions are unchanged. The transition invariant and right-congruence proof in \(\text{thm:ordered-dp}\) applies verbatim to this subcollection, and restriction cannot increase any cut's state set. Thus each side-feasibility test, together with a retained backpointer witness when it succeeds, costs
\[
 \left\{\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}
 \binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\right\}\operatorname{poly}(N).
\]
The width is still bounded by the supplied \(q_\pi\), since removing roots can only remove possible labels.

For the bounded-component algorithm of \(\text{thm:bounded-choice}\), fix an allowed root \(r\) of \(T_j\), initialize its dictionary search at \(D=S_j(r)\), and apply the same empty-locus branching search to the remaining components. If \(|D|>K\), discard this branch. Otherwise its dictionary can strictly increase at most \(K-|D|\) times, so the search has depth at most \(K\), branching factor at most \(d\), and cost \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\). The invariant from \(\text{thm:bounded-choice}\) proves that it succeeds exactly when a feasible tuple has the fixed root \(r\). Running it for the at most \(d\) roots on the requested side changes only the polynomial factor, and the first successful run returns the required witness. This proves both restricted-root algorithms and completes the theorem.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem turns orientation ambiguity into an exact, witness-bearing total-effect sensitivity analysis.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing covariance-region projections motivate effect uncertainty, but do not give this forest-specific two-value characterization or its restricted-root algorithms.
added_lemmas.consumer: SEMgraph can report whether zero, the regression ratio, or both are causally compatible, together with a root-tuple witness for each reported value.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let
\[
 \mathsf S_{\mathrm{DP}}(q,K)
 =\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q,K)}\binom qi(K-i+1).
\]
Given \((T,\Sigma,K,\pi)\), the live-label state in \(\text{def:ordered-state}\) decides \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\), decides \(\textsc{Unique-K-Fiber}\), and solves \(\textsc{Two-K-Fiber}\) exactly with at most \(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{DP}}(q_\pi,K)\) retained states per cut and \(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{DP}}(q_\pi,K)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) bit operations. In particular, this is at most \((K+1)2^{q_\pi}\operatorname{poly}(N)\), and for \(q_\pi\ge 2\) it is \(q_\pi^{O(K)}\operatorname{poly}(N)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former state count is valid but coarse. Retention forces the completed-label count to lie in \(\{0,\ldots,K-|A_\ell|\}\), yielding the displayed strict refinement while preserving all three algorithmic tasks.

prose_updates.tldr: Arbitrary Gaussian error variances identify only a Markov-equivalence class, one common variance identifies the DAG, and a supplied partial-homoscedastic partition refines the class. This project studies the missing observational regime in which the equality partition is not supplied: a faithful rational Gaussian forest covariance is compatible with a root tuple when its exact regression residuals use at most \(K\) numerical values. The supplied-order dynamic program now has the sharp state count \(\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}\binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\), preserving exact decision, uniqueness, and two-witness recovery and giving both the earlier base-two bound and a \(q_\pi^{O(K)}\) regime. The bounded-component algorithm costs \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\). For designated vertices, the population total-effect fiber is empty with the structural fiber; conditional on nonemptiness it is \(\{1\}\) on the diagonal, is \(\{0\}\) across components, and within a component is a subset of \(\{0,\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\}\). Each within-component value is present exactly when the corresponding side of the first path edge admits a feasible root, and both algorithms recover witnesses. The unrestricted \(K\)-frontier, uniqueness classification, and matching recurrence-width lower bound remain open. A covariance-region projection propagates sampling uncertainty to orientations and effects but is not claimed to be computationally efficient over the covariance region.

project_justification.fill: The project gives a root-union reduction, an exact rational tree-signature realization theorem, symbolic root loci, positive algorithms at bounded component size and bounded recurrence width, and an exact tree-effect theorem. The supplied-order algorithm uses \(\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}\binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\) states per cut; the effect theorem reduces a within-component effect fiber to two root-side feasibility queries and recovers a witness for each attainable value. The unrestricted parameterized classification and matching lower bounds remain explicit open questions whose negative branch must certify edge residuals, positive definiteness, faithfulness, rationality, and bit length before using any Gaussian gadget.

sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is needed for orientation recovery. When vertices \(x\) and \(y\) are designated, the population total-effect fiber is exactly determined by restricted root-side feasibility: within one component its only possible values are zero and \(\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\), while conditional on structural feasibility the diagonal and cross-component fibers are the singleton sets containing one and zero, respectively.

prose_updates.related_work: Peters and Buehlmann (2014) establish full identification when all innovation variances are equal, the \(K=1\) endpoint. Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019) exploit the same common-variance ordering to build scalable recovery algorithms. Wu and Drton (2023) characterize Gaussian DAG equivalence when the variance partition is supplied and therefore motivate the latent-partition step without occupying it. Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus (2026) provide rational parameter recovery, algebraic Markov descriptions, and generic faithfulness for fixed vertex colorings; the inverse theorem here instead couples every alternative root of one covariance and certifies its piecewise diagonal and off-diagonal tree-product matrix by an arbitrary-root SEM calculation. Fellows, Guo, and Kanj (2010) show that several unrestricted minimum-label graph problems are W[2]-hard, but their label systems are not Gaussian-realizable. Marx (2010) and Lampis (2025) supply decomposition and fine-grained lower-bound techniques for CSP and Set Cover interfaces. Yato and Seta (2003) and Creignou et al. (2013) show why another-solution recovery needs solution-preserving reductions and a canonical neighborhood. Strieder and Drton (2023) and Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) motivate projecting structural uncertainty to total effects; here a forest-specific path calculation first identifies the population effect fiber as at most two values and the covariance-region proposition then supplies simultaneous coverage, without an efficient optimization claim for the projection over \(M\in\mathcal C_n\).
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal target remains the feasible orientation fiber rather than an observed regression coefficient. The tree-effect theorem proves their relationship: for distinct vertices in one component, a feasible root on the \(x\)-side of the first \(x\)--\(y\) path edge directs the entire path from \(x\) to \(y\), and its directed coefficient product telescopes to the observed covariance ratio \(\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\); a feasible root on the other side yields no directed path and effect zero. Faithfulness makes the ratio nonzero, so the two memberships are distinguished exactly. The sharp ordered dynamic program and the bounded-component search test both root-side restrictions and return witnesses. The confidence projection has a different role: it contains the resulting population effect fiber with the stated probability by ranging over covariances in \(\mathcal C_n\), but no efficient method for optimizing that range is asserted.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The root-union, root-locus, bounded-choice, sharp ordered-DP, piecewise rational-tree-realization, two-witness-transfer, \(K=1\), tree-effect-fiber, and projection-coverage results are proved in this note. The ordered dynamic program uses \(\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}\binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\) states per cut and retains exact multiplicity and two witnesses. The tree-effect theorem proves that a within-component population effect fiber has at most the two values zero and \(\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\), characterizes their presence by root-side feasibility, and recovers witnesses in both positive algorithmic regimes. The headline unrestricted \(K\)-classification, the arbitrary-algorithm \(q_\pi\) lower bound, and the unrestricted uniqueness transfer remain open-ended questions. Every hardness gadget must still verify the realization theorem's hypotheses and enumerate unintended roots and auxiliary labels. The confidence projection claims simultaneous coverage, not efficient optimization over \(M\in\mathcal C_n\), likelihood-ratio calibration, unknown-mean adjustment, or robustness to approximate equality.

statement_notes.justification: The exact right congruence simultaneously gives feasibility, uniqueness, and two witnesses with a state count that adapts to both recurrence width and label budget.
statement_notes.gap: Graph-decomposition interfaces do not account for exact residual labels that retire permanently, so this state separately records the live subset and the completed-label count.
statement_notes.consumer: A supplied component order yields exact orientation and two-sided effect-witness recovery in the sharp binomial state count times \(\operatorname{poly}(N)\).

statement_notes.justification: This theorem converts structural root ambiguity into an exact two-value population total-effect sensitivity analysis.
statement_notes.gap: General covariance-region projection does not by itself expose the forest path geometry or the exact root-side membership tests.
statement_notes.consumer: SEMgraph can return zero, the covariance ratio, or both, and attach a feasible root-tuple witness to each reported effect.
